rows.premiseCheck: The discard reproduces from source at 8.0.0, 9.0.0 and HEAD; their live timeline was not re-run (no browser seat), but the source path gives the discard on its own. The investigator's cure does NOT cure G-F9-11. The fullscreen control lives only in the full layer of a start-collapsed dock, so the pointer cannot be on it when the hover morph begins, and the harness shows it is still swallowed. No banked ruling forbids narrowing the guard; unit7 RECORD:89-122 banks useDockClickIntegrity as the architectural fix whose root cause is an identity change under the pointer.
rows.grounds: Split. (1) #persistent: that region never swaps and is never a crossfade pane, so the guard's stated root cause (a layer swap put a different control under the pointer) cannot produce a press there. A persistent-scoped pass on an identity match is the narrowest cure, needs no new listener, and cures fourier's Save. (2) Arriving-layer controls (the fullscreen case): from DOM events alone, a press begun mid-morph on a freshly arrived control looks the same as race (b). A stationary pointer shows no motion, and a human approach that keeps moving shows pointermoves over the new control too. So any 'the user aimed at it' discriminator reopens the deck's gear race unless it is measured live in Chrome and Safari. The investigator's morphStartTarget arm only helps when the pointer already rested on an arriving-layer control as the morph began. On a collapsed→expanded hover that cannot happen, so the arm adds a pointermove listener for nothing. A prop that turns the guard off is declined, because it would hand every consumer a switch that reopens race (b).

rows.replyLine: ADDENDUM A-2 — split. CURE-NOW for 10.0.0, not breaking: a press on a control inside #persistent or #persistent-end passes the guard when press and click land on the same control, because that region never swaps layers. That covers your editor Save. DECLINED for the fullscreen control: it sits in the full layer of a start-collapsed dock, and a mid-morph press on a control that just arrived looks the same in the DOM as the swap race the guard exists for (a stationary pointer that the swap put over a different control). We will not add a prop that turns the guard off. For G-F9-11, wait for the dock to settle before clicking, e.g. `await expect(dock).not.toHaveAttribute("data-morphing")` before `fullscreenBtn.click()`, which your F-W10S record already names as the alternative owner. A real user's click in that ~560 ms window is deferred, and the next click on the settled dock works. Unchanged at 8.0.0, 9.0.0 and the 10.0.0 tree until the persistent cure lands.

rows.premiseCheck: Their premise holds: no banked ledger states a portal token-scope rule. The investigator's figures reproduce at HEAD and 9.0.0 but NOT at their 8.0.0 pin (44/39/10). The investigator's claim that every stamp writer teleports to <body> is wrong for CommandList, which carries the stamp but renders in place (reka ComboboxContent has no portal), so its token scope is whatever DOM parent the consumer puts it in.
rows.grounds: Custom properties inherit through the DOM tree. A portalled surface is a child of <body>, so it can inherit only :root/body declarations, and the rule is structural. The stamp marks ownership for the hold and the outside-pointer test. Re-declaring dock tokens on the stamp would mint a second token scope and is not planned. CommandList is not a portal; it follows its DOM parent.
rows.cureShape: ANSWER text: 'Token scope follows DOM ancestry. A portal the dock owns (tooltip, popover/hover-card, dropdown and submenu, select) teleports to <body>, so it is guaranteed only the --dock-* tokens declared on :root, at their :root values, plus every page-level token. At your 8.0.0 pin that is 44 :root dock tokens; at 9.0.0 and the 10.0.0 tree, 40. It inherits none of the dock-local tokens (39 at 8.0.0, 45 at 9.0.0/10.0.0: pitch/seat/run, plate tier and border, morph t, stagger, surface blur, cockpit density). For the tokens a dock re-declares over :root (10 at 8.0.0 incl. --dock-local-scale; 9 at 9.0.0/10.0.0: --dock-scale, --dock-icon-glyph, --dock-control-glyph-size, --dock-label-ratio, --dock-layer-tab-size, --dock-collapsed-padding, --dock-collapsed-summary-min-size, --dock-fg-on-aurora, --dock-active-color), it sees the :root value, not the owning dock's. Anything it must match, set on the portal content (class/style) or on :root. CommandList is the exception: it carries the stamp but does not teleport, so it inherits from wherever you mount it (inside a dock-owned popover → the :root rule; inline in the dock → the dock's tokens). data-glass-dock-portal/-owner mark ownership for the dock hold and outside-pointer test; no CSS reads them and none will.'
rows.replyLine: L-7 — ANSWER. Token scope follows DOM ancestry. A portal the dock owns (tooltip, popover/hover-card, dropdown and submenu, select) teleports to <body>, so it gets only the --dock-* tokens declared on :root, at their :root values: 44 at your 8.0.0 pin, 40 at 9.0.0 and 10.0.0. It gets none of the dock-local tokens (39 at 8.0.0, 45 later). For the tokens a dock re-declares over :root (10 at 8.0.0 including --dock-local-scale, 9 later: --dock-scale, --dock-icon-glyph, --dock-control-glyph-size, --dock-label-ratio, --dock-layer-tab-size, --dock-collapsed-padding, --dock-collapsed-summary-min-size, --dock-fg-on-aurora, --dock-active-color), it sees the :root value, not the dock's. Set anything it must match on the portal content or on :root. CommandList carries the stamp but does not teleport, so it inherits from wherever you mount it. FR-TT-9's data-glass-dock-portal/-owner stamp is ownership for the hold and the outside-pointer test. No CSS reads it at 8.0.0, 9.0.0 or 10.0.0, and it will not become a token scope.

rows.grounds: Deliberate: the uniform 8px hint pad (the --overlay-pad-hint docblock states the tight rung and retires the inline ×1.272 mint) and the caption rung (the token exists so the chip reads the house caption scale and can be retuned from :root). Incidental: the leading. The arm borrows the caption size without the caption pairing that @utility text-caption applies, so the chip rides body's 1.5. Defect: both docblocks name a text-sm backing that no longer exists, and :93 names a √φ ladder the caption rung is not on. Cure the comments and the leading; geometry and rung stay. The leading token already exists, so nothing is minted.

rows.replyLine: L-6 — CURE-NOW for 10.0.0, and a correction. The 2.00 → 0.79 ratio is stale. 2.00 was a pre-7.0.0 chip and 0.79 was the 7.0.0 chip (8px inline, 8×1.272 block). Your 8.0.0 pin, 9.0.0 and the 10.0.0 tree all pad the hint 8px on every side (--overlay-pad-hint, ratio 1.00). That pad and the --type-caption rung are deliberate, so re-baseline against them. Two things are defects. The comment at offsets.css:93-96 (not :78-82) and the list at :63 name a `text-sm` that TooltipContent has not carried since 7.0.0, and a √φ ladder the caption rung is not on; both get rewritten. And the chip sets font-size without line-height, so it inherits body's 1.5. In 10.0.0 it takes the caption's own --type-leading-caption (1.3), so a one-line hint is about 2.4px shorter at the 12px floor. Re-baseline your tooltip visuals after you re-pin to 10.0.0.
